bad_pr.title: Distinct permutations updates
bad_pr.body:
This PR brings in the algorithm changes to `distinct_permutations` from PR #399.

I've given up some micro-optimizations for algorithm clarity. This version keeps the memory usage reductions.

agent_review.authorization_note: Owner explicitly delegated autonomous case review and resulting actions to project agents.
agent_review.notes: Reviewed the complete historical test, all13 inputs, deterministic unittest lift, source lineage and explicit function-body proof. The introducing PR423 changes distinct_permutations to sort every input unconditionally; the original mixed None/int/string, bytes and tuple cases are hashable but need not be mutually orderable, so sorted raises the observed TypeError. The public parent passes the same full method. The repair copies the exact historical fallback algorithm: try sorting, then on TypeError form equality-index groups and permute their indices while preserving equivalent items. It changes34 diff lines within the verified body span and leaves the surrounding bad-tree bytes/header unchanged. Complete bad body matches historical fix-parent AST; complete repaired body matches the historical fixed AST. Original historical production diff and before/after/signature digests are bound to the machine report. Verified all9 outcomes and each bad call own introduced-line coverage, all494-test baselines, independent494x3 official suites, required probes and matching source/image/lock/CI. Fix-side PR merge92829 is honestly recorded as the second parent of integration17fd. The fix adds no public symbol, so the case-specific fix-only-symbol probe is not applicable; global tests cover that policy class. Accept this distinct regression group under the documented bounded policy. This is my authorized project-agent review, not human approval.
